messages:
jia: quick heads-up — I noticed ~18% tail latency bump for 65k+ seq requests after the last host-staging heuristic landed. looks like fragmentation plus extra memcpy on evict paths. attaching rough logs.
mike: can you paste the logs? or sample timeline? curious if it's queuing or copy cost.
jia: logs (trimmed):\n```
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] req=0x7f8a seq=65536 stage_alloc fail -> fallback memcpy(12.3ms)
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] evict: candidate=poolA size=1.2MB frag=0.78 freelist_scan=4 loops
[2026-03-18T21:12:03Z] kv-cache hit=0 miss=1 delayed_reclaim=8
```\nseems failing to find contiguous host staging region, then we copy from GPU -> host, which spikes tail.
dmitri: that matches what I saw locally. fragmentation in the staging arena means we end up splitting and memcpy'ing per-chunk. idea: introduce a sparse staging buffer + "evict-delta" API so runtime can express partial-slot eviction without forcing a full linear copy.
eva: can you sketch the API? curious about semantics and how it interacts with prefix kv cache.
dmitri: rough sketch:\n```
// reserve space in sparse staging, returns handle
sparse_reserve(pool, bytes, flags) -> handle
// attach an eviction delta describing ranges and small metadata
evict_delta(handle, [ {gpu_offset, length, delta_type} ... ]) -> status
// finalize (commit or rollback)
sparse_commit(handle) | sparse_abort(handle)
```\nSemantics: delta entries represent subranges that will be materialized lazily to host pages; no need to find a contiguous host slab up-front.
mike: tradeoffs? sounds more complex in allocator and hazard tracking.
dmitri: yeah. pros: avoids big contiguous host allocs and big memcpy, reduces fragmentation pressure. cons: more metadata, slow path when many small deltas — can increase CPU churn and bookkeeping.
jia: two operational concerns: 1) we must preserve eviction ordering so GPU ops reading cache don't race with deltas, 2) rollback path on error must be cheap.
eva: also need to think about KV cache: if a prefix is cached and we only evict partial ranges, hits must be consistent. either we invalidate whole key or support partial invalidation. partial invalidation may break downstream assumptions.
mike: microbench I ran last night with a prototype: 8KB avg chunk, 128MB working set, compare current baseline vs sparse-proto: memory usage -2.4%, token throughput -0.6% (negl), CPU sys up +12% during GC windows, tail latency p99 down 14% in long seq test.
sam: that p99 drop is promising. what's the deploy risk? do we need feature flag and per-customer kill switch?
dmitri: feature flag + incremental rollout. starts as opt-in per-model. runtime will expose config: sparse_enabled, max_delta_per_req, metadata_mem_limit.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline note: if you add new DB schema for handle metadata, coordinate migration with infra team. see infra/guides/db-migrations.
jia: implementation detail: prefer off-heap metadata region per-GPU node to avoid cross-node GC stalls. also consider compacting delta lists during low load.
dmitri: compaction strategy: coalesce adjacent deltas into ranges when total metadata bytes > threshold or at low load. heuristics: coalesce if adjacent_gaps < 4KB.
eva: monitoring: we should emit metrics: sparse.delta_count, sparse.coalesces, sparse.rollback_rate, staging.fragmentation_ratio, sparse.cpu_ms_per_gc.
mike: and add tracing spans for reserve->evict->commit so we can tie tail latency to specific steps.
sam: ops: plan for a canary run on Dedicated clusters where we can toggle per-customer. timeline?
jia: I'll prototype reserve/commit in the allocator shim this week. dmitri can own API shape and metadata layout. mike can run microbench harness on Friday.
dmitri: ack. I'll post an RFC PR with API and state machine tonight.
eva: will draft dashboard widgets for the metrics mentioned.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled if RFC lands and tests pass. CI job: alloc-sparse-proto/test-evict, perf/regression/long-seq.
jia: action items: (1) dmitri RFC PR, (2) mike perf harness test cases, (3) eva dashboards, (4) jia prototype allocator shim. tagging @sam for rollout plan.\n:+1: thanks all.
